newsitem.title: USA: Clinton leads tribute to teachers' chief Shanker.
newsitem.headline: Clinton leads tribute to teachers' chief Shanker.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday led a memorial tribute to teachers' union leader Albert Shanker, who he said had helped to inspire his crusade for higher learning standards.

"Today education is the number one priority of the American people. Al Shanker helped to make it so," Clinton told friends and co-workers of the president of the American Federation of Teachers, who died of cancer Feb. 22.

The AFT represents 907,000 elementary and secondary school teachers, school-related personnel, higher education faculty, nurses and other health professionals as well as state and local government employees. Shanker led the AFT for 23 years.
At the service on the campus of George Washington University, Clinton said Shanker wanted teachers to lead the way in fostering international understanding.
He announced that teachers who participated in such international programmes in civic education would be designated Shanker Fellows.
Clinton said another element of Shanker's legacy would be the voluntary national testing of 4th grade reading and 8th grade math skills that he has been promoting and which is due to start in 1999.

"He thought that this whole standards movement was essential for democracy to work, that it was the only way to give every child without regard to his or her background a chance to live up to his or her God-given capacity," Clinton said.
